original_question: For a real Hénon map, does the closure of the set of periodic orbits support every invariant probability measure of the map?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s intended open problem very closely: it asks whether, for a real Hénon map, the periodic dynamics is rich enough to account for every invariant probability measure. The logical form and the main objects are essentially the same as in the paper’s official formulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03907))
missing_details: The relevant family in this part of the paper is the quadratic real Hénon family f_{c,b}(x,y) = (x^2 + c - by, x), so the map should be specified in that section’s notation rather than left as an unspecified real dynamical system. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03907))
The ambient phase space is R^2, and the parameters c,b are real; the quantifier is over every map in this real quadratic Hénon family. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03907))

Question 10 itself does not impose extra assumptions such as mild dissipation, zero entropy, or renormalizability; those appear only in the surrounding discussion as known cases or neighboring problems. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03907))

To make the statement fully stand-alone, the phrase 'the closure of the set of periodic orbits supports all the invariant probability measures' should be made explicit as: for every invariant probability measure μ, one has supp(μ) ⊂ closure(Per(f_{c,b})). The sentence immediately before Question 10 supplies this intended meaning by stating density of periodic points in the union of supports of invariant probability measures. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03907))
If one introduces notation, Per(f_{c,b}) should be defined as the set of periodic points of f_{c,b}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03907))
refined_question: Let f_{c,b}: R^2 → R^2 be a real quadratic Hénon map, f_{c,b}(x,y) = (x^2 + c - by, x), with b,c ∈ R. Is it true that every f_{c,b}-invariant Borel probability measure μ satisfies supp(μ) ⊂ closure(Per(f_{c,b})), where Per(f_{c,b}) denotes the set of periodic points of f_{c,b}? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03907))
justification: The draft is targeting Question 10 of §3.3 rather than a broader neighboring problem, because the paper asks almost verbatim whether, for any real Hénon map, the closure of periodic orbits supports all invariant probability measures. The section-wide notation needed to make that question self-contained is introduced earlier in §3.1, where the relevant family is f_{c,b}(x,y) = (x^2 + c - by, x). The sentence immediately preceding Question 10 gives the key nearby context: for mildly dissipative real Hénon maps, periodic points are dense in the union of the supports of invariant probability measures, which clarifies the intended meaning of the open problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03907))
